caption:

3 common mistakes:

❌ Just “image”

title: Selittävä
alt: Accessibility basics. What is alt text? And why the images on your site need it. Swipe
In short. A picture, described in words. Alt text says what’s in an image. It isn’t shown on the page, but a screen reader reads it out loud. Screen reader says. “Black knee-length wool coat”

Who it’s for. 55,000. people in Finland are visually impaired. Some of them use the web with a screen reader, which reads the page out loud. Source: estimate by the Finnish Federation of the Visually Impaired and THL.
The problem. Without alt text, a customer may hear: “image” “IMG_2041.jpg” …or nothing at all. They never learn what’s in the picture.

The fix. The fix is one sentence. 1. Open the image in your site editor. 2. Find the field called “Alt text” or “Alternative text”. 3. Write what the picture shows. Then the screen reader says. “Black knee-length wool coat”
What about your site? Are your images missing alt text? Selkeo checks your site every week and tells you what to fix first. See your score now.
caption:
What is alt text, and why should you care?

It’s a short description of an image. It isn’t shown on the page, but a screen reader reads it out loud to a customer who can’t see the picture.

No alt text? They may hear a file name, or nothing.

The fix is one sentence:
1. Open the image in your site editor
2. Find the “Alt text” field
3. Write what the picture shows

title: Arjen esimerkit
alt: Three everyday examples. Your lunch menu is an image. Not everyone can see it. Three common situations and a fix for each. Swipe

Example 1 · Lunch menu as an image. LUNCH 11–2. Mon. Salmon soup. Tue. Beef stew. Wed. Veggie lasagne. lunch_week47.jpg. A screen reader may say. “lunch_week47.jpg” The fix. Put the menu on the page as text. The image can stay next to it.
Example 2 · Product photo. IMG_2041.jpg. Wool coat. €189. A screen reader may say. “IMG_2041.jpg” The fix. Alt text: “Black wool coat, knee-length, double-breasted”.
Example 3 · An offer as an image. −20%. Winter coats until Sunday. banner_final2.png. A screen reader may say. “banner_final2.png” The fix. Alt text: “Winter coats 20% off until Sunday”.
Recognize your own site? What do the images on your site say? Selkeo checks your site every week and tells you if images are missing alt text. See your score now.
caption:
3 everyday images that leave some customers with nothing:

1. The lunch menu as an image → put it on the page as text
2. A product photo with no alt text → describe what’s in it
3. An offer as an image → write the offer into the alt text

Text inside an image doesn’t reliably reach a screen reader.

title: Tekninen
alt: WCAG 1.1.1 · Level A. The alt attribute: 4 cases, 4 right answers. Informative, decorative, linked, and text in images. Swipe
Case 1 · Informative image. The image says something. . A screen reader says, for example. “Black knee-length wool coat” Alt carries the same information the image gives a sighted user.
Case 2 · Decorative image. The image is pure decoration. . Screen reader. Skips the image. Empty alt, not missing alt. With a missing alt attribute, a screen reader may read the file name.

Case 3 · Image as a link. The icon goes somewhere. . A screen reader says, for example. “Cart, link” Say where the link goes. Don’t describe the icon. Google uses a linked image’s alt text as the link’s anchor text.

Case 4 · Text in an image. Lunch menu, offer, opening hours.

Lunch 11–2

  • Mon: salmon soup
. If text can be real text, make it text. WCAG 1.4.5, Level AA.
Good to know. Automation finds missing alt text. Not bad alt text. Selkeo runs axe-core checks every week. Whether the text is any good takes a human. See your score now.
caption:
The alt attribute in 4 cases (WCAG 1.1.1, Level A):

1. Informative image → alt carries the same information
2. Decorative image → alt="" (empty, not missing)
3. Linked image → alt says where the link goes. Google uses it as anchor text
4. Text in an image → if it can be real text, make it text (WCAG 1.4.5, Level AA)

Automated checks find missing alt text. Whether it’s any good takes a human.

title: Tarkistuslista
alt: Save this. Alt text checklist. Every informative image has alt text. Decorative images have an empty alt. A linked image’s alt says where the link goes. Text is on the page as text, not as an image. Alt doesn’t start with “image of”. Go through it before you publish.
caption:
A 5-point alt text checklist:

1. Every informative image has alt text
2. Decorative images have an empty alt
3. A linked image’s alt says where the link goes
4. Text is on the page as text, not as an image
5. Alt doesn’t start with “image of”. The screen reader already says it’s an image

Save it and run through it before you publish 📌

title: Sanasto
alt: Accessibility glossary. alt text. alt · text · noun. 1. A picture described in words. Not shown on the page, but a screen reader reads it out loud. 2. The text shown in place of an image that fails to load. E.g. “Black knee-length wool coat”
caption:
Accessibility glossary: alt text.

A picture described in words. Not shown on the page, but a screen reader reads it out loud. It also appears in place of an image that fails to load.
